title: Palabruno: From Early Prototype to Launch
description: Built and launched a React web workspace and React Native apps for Spanish learners and teachers, including an interactive reader, student and group management, sharing, and subscriptions.
seoTitle: Palabruno Project | Spanish Reading MVP Launch
seoDescription: React web and React Native mobile engineering for Palabruno: an interactive Spanish reader, teacher workflows, subscriptions, and cross-platform launch.
role: MVP scope, AI reader compiler, learner and teacher workflows, payments, launch, and handoff
deliveryHighlights: Spanish reader compiler combining NLP, linguistic rules, constrained generation, and regression evaluations
Durable text processing with persisted progress and per-stage cost and latency tracking
Learner mobile apps and teacher web workspace with RevenueCat and Stripe payments
Public site, store assets, release steps, and founder handoff
outcomes: Launched iOS, Android, and web surfaces
Connected mobile subscriptions through RevenueCat and teacher payments through Stripe
Gave the founder a tutor-first offer ready to test with real Spanish teachers
constraints: The founder had an early prototype but needed help deciding what belonged in the first paid version.
The product had to serve two connected audiences: individual Spanish learners on mobile and teachers managing students from the web.
The MVP needed real payments and app-store readiness.
Late-stage feedback kept surfacing across UX, pricing, legal copy, performance, screenshots, and store-review requirements.
problem: Palabruno began with an early prototype for a Spanish reader. Learners could tap a word for translation, grammar, and pronunciation help without leaving the text.
The open question was who would pay first. Tutors already created lesson material and sent it to students, which made them the first buyer worth testing.
Because the founder was nontechnical, the work also covered scope decisions, user experience, payments, store launches, public copy, and handoff documentation.
solution: I split the MVP into two connected products: a mobile reader for students and a web workspace for tutors.
The mobile app focused on reading. Learners could import or generate Spanish texts, get help in context, save material, and upgrade to Premium through the app stores.
The web workspace let tutors create readings from lesson notes, manage students and groups, share material, and track recent shares.
Free, Premium, and Teacher each had a distinct role. RevenueCat handled mobile Premium subscriptions, while Stripe handled Teacher payments on the web.
I also completed the public site, legal pages, store listings, screenshots, release docs, public copy, and founder handoff.
result: Palabruno moved from an early prototype to launch: the iOS app went live on the App Store, the Android app went live on Google Play, and the public web product was ready for real users.
Premium subscriptions run through Apple and Google via RevenueCat. Teacher payments run through Stripe on the web.

The founder ended the engagement with a working cross-platform product, tutor workspace, shared backend, launch documentation, store assets, and a tutor-first offer to test with real Spanish teachers.
